question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.9)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.48)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0).$
question.worked_solution:
By the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.9),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.9,\,P(X=0)=0.1,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.48),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.48,\,P(Y=0)=0.52.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.1+0.52-0.1\cdot 0.52 \\  & =0.62-0.052 \\  & =0.568.\end{aligned}
$$
